title: Roadmap to AI Adoption in Healthcare — June 2026 Edition

citations.claim: Health data is special-category data under GDPR Article 9: processing is prohibited unless a specific Article 9(2) condition applies, on top of an Article 6 lawful basis.
citations.publisher: Official Journal of the European Union

citations.claim: Software intended to inform diagnosis or treatment is a medical device that must be CE-marked under the EU Medical Device Regulation (EU) 2017/745 before being placed on the market.
citations.publisher: Official Journal of the European Union

citations.claim: The MHRA regulates software and AI as a medical device in the UK and has set out a programme to reform how such products are regulated.
citations.publisher: Medicines and Healthcare products Regulatory Agency

citations.claim: The EU AI Act classifies AI systems that are, or are a safety component of, a regulated medical device as high-risk, attaching risk-management, data-governance, logging and human-oversight obligations to the deployer.
citations.publisher: Official Journal of the European Union

citations.claim: The NIST AI Risk Management Framework organises trustworthy-AI practice into four functions — Govern, Map, Measure, Manage — that healthcare deployers adapt as the backbone of an AI governance programme.
citations.publisher: National Institute of Standards and Technology
